newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Juppe at new low in poll.
newsitem.headline: France's Juppe at new low in poll.

text.p: French voters' confidence in Prime Minister Alain Juppe has tumbled to an all-time low amid deep gloom about the economy, an opinion poll showed on Friday.

The Sofres survey for the weekly Le Figaro Magazine found just 27 percent of those questioned had confidence in conservative Juppe in late September against 34 a month earlier. The numbers lacking confidence rose to 71 percent from 69.
"There's persistent gloom in France about the economy. Juppe gets most of the blame," said Didier Witkowski of Sofres' political studies department.
He said many people also felt cheated by small income tax cuts trumpeted by Juppe for 1997 when a host of other levies were set to rise.

Thirty-seven percent said they had confidence in President Jacques Chirac in the poll of 1,000 people conducted from September 25 to 27, down three points from August. Sixty-one percent had little or no confidence, a gain of three points.
The magazine said that only Pierre Mauroy, prime minister in 1981-84 and Edith Cresson, premier in 1991-92, had recorded such a low score as Juppe in the Sofres poll. Both are Socialists.
Witkowski said Juppe's support had eroded sharply even among supporters of the ruling centre-right alliance. He now had the confidence of just half of coalition voters.
Juppe, who took office in May 1995, won an unenthusiastic vote of confidence on Wednesday from parliament, where his coalition controls four-fifths of the seats.
